node.title: Re: @INC error
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
According to your Perl script that prints [doc://@INC], you appear to be using [mod://local::lib], but those paths (/home/jrayner/perl5/lib/perl5/...) don't appear in the error message, so those two runs of perl are different. Since your script appears to be called ~/CRON/email-reminder-2.0.pl, note that [man://cron] does not provide a full environment to the code it runs, so if you want perl scripts run from cron to pick up on the modules you've installed in a nonstandard location, one way to do that is to explicitly set the PERL5LIB environment variable in your [man://crontab;5|crontab] file. I'd also recommend always using absolute pathnames for everything in your crontab, including the perl binary.

Or, you could point PERL5LIB at /usr/local/share/perl5/, as [hippo] [id://11111446|pointed out]. I'm a little confused as to how the module ended up there though - your standard [doc://@INC] paths contains /usr/local/share/perl5/5.30, so going by that the module should have been installed to /usr/local/share/perl5/5.30/Mail/Mailer.pm. Are you using the standard installation procedures for the modules (the system package manager, or e.g. [mod://cpanm]) or are you doing something custom?
